notes: Formula (I), the 1,3-dione (triketone) form. This is one of a set of three structures drawn one under another between [0002] and [0003]; (I), (I') and (I") are recorded as three separate drawings entries so each keeps its own printed formula label, but they are one tautomer set and paragraph [0002] presents them as such. Read at 6x magnification: all three C=O bonds are unambiguously double (two parallel lines each) and C2 of the ring bears a hydrogen with single bonds on both sides, so the ring is the saturated 1,3-dione and nothing is enolised. The formula label is printed '(I)'. The text layer reduced this whole drawing to 'O / O / C / o1 Ner, / O / 2 / / / 4. Y-H,', from which nothing chemical is recoverable; every atom, bond and ring position here comes from the image. SMILES hand-checked atom by atom against the drawing and against the name: C17H16ClF3O6S, 6 oxygens (2 ring ketone, 1 benzoyl ketone, 2 sulfonyl, 1 ether). presented_as: none of the four documented values fits. This is not a route and not an intermediate; it is the invention's own active substance, whose polymorphs the patent claims, so 'invention_active_substance' is used rather than forcing 'unclear' onto something the page states plainly. Flagged for a human to normalise if the enum is meant to be closed.

notes: Formula (I'), an enol tautomer, and the drawing settles it without ambiguity, so a SMILES is given. Which oxygen carries the H: the oxygen on ring carbon C3, the lower of the two ring oxygens as drawn, which is labelled 'OH' in full rather than as a bare O. Which bond is drawn double: the endocyclic C2=C3 bond, two clearly separated parallel lines checked at 6x. Which carbonyl is enolised: a RING carbonyl, the one at C3; the other ring carbonyl at C1 is still drawn C=O and the exocyclic benzoyl C=O is untouched. So (I') differs from (I) by moving the C2 hydrogen of (I) onto the C3 oxygen and making C2=C3 double. Confidence is high because both the OH label and the doubled ring edge are legible and separated; there is no place where a guess was needed. Aryl half is identical to (I), substituent for substituent, checked independently on this drawing and not copied from (I). The text layer gave 'O / O / C / o1 Ner, / O / OH / sa / M \, / O CH' for this structure; only the 'OH' survived in it, and even that carries no position. SMILES hand-checked: C17H16ClF3O6S, same formula as (I) as a tautomer must be. See the (I) entry for the presented_as caveat.

notes: Formula (I"), the other enol tautomer, and this drawing is also unambiguous, so a SMILES is given. Which oxygen carries the H: the EXOCYCLIC oxygen, the one on the former benzoyl carbon, labelled 'OH' at the top of the drawing between the ring and the Cl. Which bond is drawn double: the EXOCYCLIC C2=C bond between ring carbon C2 and that carbon, two clearly separated parallel lines checked at 6x. Which carbonyl is enolised: the exocyclic one; both ring carbonyls at C1 and C3 are still drawn C=O, which is the visible difference from (I') and the reason the two enols cannot be confused. So (I") differs from (I) by moving the C2 hydrogen of (I) onto the exocyclic oxygen and making the exocyclic bond double. GEOMETRY NOT RECORDED IN THE SMILES: the exocyclic C=C is drawable as E or Z and the drawing does show one particular planar arrangement, with the OH on the same side as the C1 ring carbonyl (consistent with an intramolecular hydrogen bond, though the page draws no such bond). Nothing in the text designates E or Z, so the SMILES is written without double-bond stereochemistry rather than asserting a configuration the patent does not claim. Connectivity is high confidence; the configuration is deliberately left unspecified and is called out here so it is not mistaken for an omission. The text layer gave 'O / OH / Cl / 21 / o1 Ner, / / Yh / 3'; the stray '21' and '3' are fragments of the drawing, not text. SMILES hand-checked: C17H16ClF3O6S, same formula as (I) and (I'). See the (I) entry for the presented_as caveat.
